title: What is a unit of competency?
description: A unit of competency is a published standard for one work function: elements, performance criteria and assessment requirements. Structure and an example.
shortAnswer: A unit of competency is a published standard that describes one work function in terms of the outcomes a competent person achieves and the evidence needed to prove it. In Australia's vocational system each unit sets out elements (essential outcomes), performance criteria (the performance that shows each element is achieved), foundation skills, and separate assessment requirements covering performance evidence, knowledge evidence and assessment conditions. Units are the building blocks of nationally recognized qualifications.
keyTakeaways: A unit of competency describes one work function, not a course or a qualification.
Elements state essential outcomes; performance criteria state the observable performance that demonstrates each element.
Each unit has a companion Assessment Requirements document listing performance evidence, knowledge evidence and assessment conditions.
Australia's training.gov.au publishes units with a code, release history and mapping to the units they supersede.
The structure is a useful template for any organization writing its own competency standards, whether or not it uses the Australian system.

sections.heading: Where are units of competency used?

blocks.text: Units of competency are the core building block of Australia's vocational education and training (VET) system. They are published in training packages on the national register, [training.gov.au](https://training.gov.au/training/details/BSBWHS311/unitdetails), and registered training organizations must assess against them. The Australian Skills Quality Authority (ASQA) [Assessment Practice Guide](https://www.asqa.gov.au/for-providers/standards-for-RTOs/practice-guides/quality-area-1-training-and-assessment/assessment-practice-guide) expects an assessment system that "determines what competence looks like based on the unit elements, performance criteria and assessment requirements".

The term is Australian, but the idea is general: a unit is a portable, assessable standard for one function. Organizations elsewhere use the same structure inside a [competency framework](/glossary/competency-framework), and it underpins [competency-based training](/glossary/competency-based-training) in any market.

sections.heading: What are the parts of a unit of competency?

blocks.text: A unit has a fixed set of fields. The table uses the national unit BSBWHS311 Assist with maintaining workplace safety, from the Business Services Training Package, as published on training.gov.au.

blocks.text: The unit itself defines the terms. In the [BSBWHS311 unit document](https://training.gov.au/assets/BSB/BSBWHS311_R1.pdf), "Elements describe the essential outcomes" and "Performance criteria describe the performance needed to demonstrate achievement of the element." Release 1 was first released with the Business Services Training Package Version 7.0.

sections.heading: What do the assessment requirements of a unit specify?

blocks.text: The assessment requirements specify exactly what a candidate must do and know, and the conditions under which assessment must happen. They are what turns a unit into a [competency assessment](/glossary/competency-assessment) plan.

items: **Performance evidence:** the tasks the candidate must complete, often with a volume. BSBWHS311 requires the candidate to assist with implementing and monitoring "at least three different" safety policies or procedures in a work team's processes.
**Knowledge evidence:** what the candidate must know, such as hazard identification procedures, the hierarchy of control measures, and organizational safety policies.

**Assessment conditions:** the environment and resources required, such as access to safety processes, procedures and workplace equipment, and a statement that assessors must meet the assessor requirements in applicable VET legislation, frameworks or standards.

blocks.text: These requirements are read together with the principles of assessment and [rules of evidence](/glossary/rules-of-evidence), which govern how the evidence is gathered and judged. The [BSBWHS311 assessment requirements](https://training.gov.au/assets/BSB/BSBWHS311_AssessmentRequirements_R1.pdf) are published as their own document for each release.

sections.heading: How is a unit of competency different from a course or a learning outcome?

blocks.text: A unit of competency defines the standard; a course is one way of preparing someone to meet it. The same unit can be delivered through classroom training, on-the-job coaching, or no training at all where existing skill is recognized through [recognition of prior learning](/glossary/recognition-of-prior-learning). A [learning outcome](/glossary/learning-outcomes) is narrower and course-specific; a unit is an industry-agreed workplace standard with its own evidence rules.

sections.heading: How can an organization write an internal competency in unit format?

blocks.text: Illustrative example: an internal competency for a pharmacy technician, "Process a controlled medicine order", written in the same structure. It is not a national unit.

head: Element
Performance criteria
Performance evidence
Knowledge evidence
rows: 1. Verify the order
1.1 Confirm prescriber authority; 1.2 Check quantity against limits in the procedure
Verify five orders, including one that must be rejected
Prescriber authority rules; quantity limits
2. Record the transaction
2.1 Complete the register entry at the time of supply; 2.2 Reconcile stock
Two complete register entries reviewed by a supervisor
Register requirements; reconciliation steps
3. Escalate discrepancies
3.1 Identify a discrepancy; 3.2 Report it within the required time
One simulated discrepancy handled
Escalation route and timeframes

blocks.text: Writing internal standards this way forces three decisions that informal role descriptions skip: what the observable outcomes are, how much evidence is enough, and what knowledge must be checked separately.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry models units of competency, or internal standards written in the same shape, as framework entries with elements, criteria and evidence requirements linked to assessment points. When a unit is superseded, the mapping shows which content and assessments must be reviewed.

faqs.q: What is the difference between an element and a performance criterion?
faqs.a: An element is an essential outcome of the work function, such as contributing to consultation on safety. Performance criteria break each element into the specific, observable performance that shows the outcome has been achieved. Assessors judge evidence against the performance criteria, read together with the assessment requirements.

faqs.q: What happens when a unit of competency is updated?
faqs.a: A new release or a new code is published with mapping information. BSBWHS311, for example, records that it supersedes and is equivalent to BSBWHS301. Training providers then follow transition rules, and organizations that use the unit internally should review linked content, assessments and records against the new version.

faqs.q: Can an employer use national units of competency for internal training?
faqs.a: Yes. The published content can be used as a reference for internal standards, assessment design and job descriptions. Nationally recognized qualifications and statements of attainment, however, are issued by registered training organizations regulated against the national Standards. An employer using a unit internally issues only its own internal competency record.

faqs.q: Is a unit of competency the same as a skill in a skills taxonomy?
faqs.a: No. A skills taxonomy entry names and describes a skill so it can be tagged and searched. A unit of competency is an assessable standard for a whole work function, with defined outcomes, performance criteria and evidence requirements. A single unit usually draws on several taxonomy skills.
